references.text: The bronze sockets for the tabernacle and the courtyard are also mentioned here, fulfilling the original instruction in Exod 38:20.
Refers to the sockets of the tabernacle and the courtyard along with their cords as part of the materials that were to be gathered.
Describes how the sockets for the tabernacle and the surrounding courtyard were made from bronze taken from the base of the bronze altar.
Mentions the sockets as part of the completed work on the tabernacle that was brought to Moses.
The responsibility of the Kohathites included the pillars around the courtyard with their bases, sockets, and cords.
The Merarites were responsible for carrying the pillars, bases, sockets, and cords of the courtyard.
Highlights the theological distinction between the lower parts (bronze) and the upper parts (silver) in the construction of the sanctuary.
